note: Day 1 · intro (pin manually after it goes out)
text:
gm. Marketer by day, builder by night.

I'm building Holdrs, a token launchpad on Robinhood Chain. The team is me and a few AI tools.

Click to launch. Hold to earn.

Testnet first. I'll share everything here: progress, mistakes, numbers.

Follow along 🌙

12 years in marketing. I've launched a lot of products. None of them were mine.

Holdr is the first one that is.

I still have a full-time job. Holdrs gets my nights and weekends.

Anyone else building something on the side? How do you keep going?

Holdrs started as a wallet. I shipped it.

Then I had to admit it: nobody needs another wallet. People already trust theirs.

So I deleted it and kept the part people want.

Loving your code isn't the same as building a product. What have you had to let go of?

The Holdrs team: me and AI.

I decide what to build, what to cut, and what the rules are. AI helps me write it.

Then we try to break it. 200 contract tests. One full testnet run: launch to graduation, 19 transactions.

What would you build with AI?

Every trade on Holdrs has a 1% fee.

0.7% goes to whoever launched the token. 0.3% to the platform. Before graduation and after.

If you build the community, you should share in what it makes.

Creators: what would you do with the fees?

Maybe unpopular: holding should be fun again.

Right now the game is speed. Snipe, flip, leave.

On Holdrs, the longer you hold, the more points you collect. Day 7: ×1.5. Day 30: ×2.

What's the longest you've ever held a token?
